question: Which of the following fundamental rights has been amended as a constitutional right in the form of Article 300A in the new Chapter IV Part XII of the Indian Constitution?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Right to Property**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Right to Property** was originally a fundamental right under Article 31 of the Indian Constitution.
 
• However, the 44th Amendment Act of 1978 removed the Right to Property from the list of fundamental rights.
 
• It was then made a constitutional right under Article 300A in the new Chapter IV of Part XII of the Constitution.
 
• Article 300A states that no person shall be deprived of his property save by authority of law.
 
• This change was made to reduce the burden on the judiciary and to facilitate the process of land acquisition for public purposes.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Article 31** was part of the original Constitution adopted on 26th November 1949.
 
• The **44th Amendment Act** was enacted during the Janata Party government led by Morarji Desai.
 
• The amendment aimed to balance the state's power to acquire property with the individual's right to hold property, without the stringent protections associated with fundamental rights.
 
• This amendment reflects the evolving nature of the Indian Constitution to address contemporary socio-economic needs.
 
• Other fundamental rights continue to be protected under Part III of the Constitution, ensuring justice, equality, and liberty for all citizens.
